title: Questionnaire flow overview
purpose: Set the eight steps, their order and when each applies, how the employee saves, resumes, reviews and submits, and what happens to answers that no longer apply or need changing after submission.

stories.title: Show the source tax step only to employees who are subject to source tax
stories.i_want: the source tax details (denomination, whether the spouse works, whether there are children) to be asked only of employees who are subject to source tax
stories.so_that: I no longer have to work out up front who must answer these questions, and employees who are not subject to source tax are not asked for personal data no party needs
stories.priority_reason: HR names this as a daily pain ('I never know up front who has to answer those questions'), and asking everyone would break data minimisation (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Source tax details are asked only of employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered where they live and, if they live in Switzerland, their nationality, C permit, civil status and the spouse questions that apply to them
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire decides whether to show step 6 'Source tax details'
acceptance_criteria.then: step 6 is shown only when the employee is subject to source tax under HR's rule: everyone living abroad, whatever their nationality, and people living in Switzerland who are not Swiss, have no C permit and are not married to (or in a registered partnership with) a Swiss national or C-permit holder living in Switzerland. 'Here' in HR's wording is read as Switzerland and anyone with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: HR's consolidated rule is applied as stated.

examples.name: Maria, Portuguese with a C permit (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-845204)
Tomás, Brazilian with a B permit, Swiss wife, living in Winterthur (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-b90bd9)
Swiss citizen living abroad like Stefan (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a); country of residence assumed to be Germany
Non-Swiss single employee without C permit living in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents in principle not liable skip the source tax details
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee lives in Liechtenstein and has answered the cross-border questions in step 5
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire decides whether to show step 6 'Source tax details'
acceptance_criteria.then: step 6 is skipped when the employee returns daily to Liechtenstein or expects at most 45 non-return days (in principle no source tax liability); it is shown when the employee expects more than 45 non-return days. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the cross-border questions come before denomination, spouse and children for Liechtenstein residents.

examples.name: Liechtenstein resident, no daily return, at most 45 non-return days
Liechtenstein resident, more than 45 non-return days

stories.title: Ask the steps in an order that avoids unneeded questions
stories.i_want: to go through the onboarding questionnaire in eight fixed steps, in English, where each step and question appears only when it applies to me
stories.so_that: I answer only what a receiving party needs for me, and the answers that decide later questions (where I live, nationality, civil status) come first
stories.priority_reason: The step order is the backbone of the questionnaire; without it no registration data is collected (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Eight steps in a fixed order
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee opens the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they go through it
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire is in English and has exactly these steps in this order: 1 About you, 2 Home address, 3 Nationality and C permit, 4 Civil status and spouse, 5 Cross-border commuting, 6 Source tax details, 7 Children, 8 Permit reminder, summary and submission. There is no separate step for the first working day. A step that does not apply to the employee is skipped. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: this step list and order.

acceptance_criteria.title: Steps 1 and 2 are asked of everyone; the canton only of Swiss residents
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in steps 1 'About you' and 2 'Home address'
acceptance_criteria.then: first name, last name, date of birth and first working day are required from everyone; street, house number (or 'no house number'), postcode, town and country of the home address that applies on the first working day are required from everyone; the canton is asked only when the country is Switzerland. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the address is the one on the first working day and every address field is required.

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 3 only for employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: step 3 'Nationality and C permit' is reached
acceptance_criteria.then: nationality is asked only of employees living in Switzerland; whether they hold a C permit is asked only if they are not Swiss. Employees living abroad skip step 3.

examples.name: Maria, Portuguese with a C permit (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-845204)

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 4 civil status from everyone, spouse questions only where needed
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reaches step 4 'Civil status and spouse'
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer their civil status
acceptance_criteria.then: civil status is required from everyone, wherever they live; the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth is asked of married, registered-partner and separated employees; the spouse's nationality and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland are asked only of non-Swiss employees without a C permit living in Switzerland who are married or in a registered partnership, and the spouse's C permit only if the spouse is not Swiss. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: separated and registered-partner employees are entered at the fund as Married.

examples.name: Tomás, Brazilian with a B permit, Swiss wife (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-b90bd9)
Separated non-Swiss employee without C permit in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 5 only for employees living in Liechtenstein or Germany
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: step 5 'Cross-border commuting' is reached
acceptance_criteria.then: employees living in Liechtenstein are asked about daily return and, without daily return, about more than 45 non-return days; employees living in Germany are asked the German cross-border questions (daily return, and depending on it the certificate of residence or non-return days); everyone else skips step 5. The employee states what they expect for the year.

acceptance_criteria.title: Steps 6 and 7 only for employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the questionnaire has determined whether the employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: steps 6 'Source tax details' and 7 'Children' are reached
acceptance_criteria.then: step 6 (denomination; whether the spouse is gainfully employed, only for married employees and registered partners; whether there are children) is shown only to employees subject to source tax, except Liechtenstein residents in principle not liable; step 7 (one block per child, no maximum number of children) is shown only when step 6 is shown and the employee has children. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: there is no maximum number of children.

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 8 is shown to everyone
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has completed the steps that apply to them
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the end of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: step 8 shows the permit reminder where it applies, the summary of all answers and the single confirmation to submit.

stories.title: Ask each piece of information once and reuse it for every receiving party
stories.i_want: each piece of information to be asked of the employee only once and reused for the pension fund, source tax and HR
stories.so_that: I no longer collect the same data several times or chase spouse details by email, and the employee is not asked the same thing twice
stories.priority_reason: Asking once and reusing is the core promise of the feature (G-01); HR's email chasing for spouse details 'takes forever'.

acceptance_criteria.title: One answer serves every party that needs it
acceptance_criteria.given: an answer is needed by more than one receiving party (for example civil status for the pension fund and for source tax, or the home address country for HR, source tax and the fund's canton)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers it
acceptance_criteria.then: the question appears once in the questionnaire and the same answer is recorded for every party that needs it; the source tax questions 'main residence in Switzerland?' and 'country of residence' are taken from the home address country and not asked again.

acceptance_criteria.title: A question is asked only when a party needs it for this person
acceptance_criteria.given: no receiving party needs a given answer for this employee
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: that question is not asked, and values Lonio can derive (such as the insurance start date from the first working day) are derived rather than asked.

examples.name: Swiss citizen living abroad like Stefan (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a); country of residence assumed to be Germany

stories.title: Remind non-Swiss employees and employees living abroad to bring their permit
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to remind every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad, at the end, to bring their permit on the first working day
stories.so_that: fewer new employees forget their permit on day one
stories.priority_reason: An explicit HR wish ('Half of them forget'); it blocks no registration and collects no data.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who sees the permit reminder
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered where they live and, if they live in Switzerland, their nationality
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach step 8 'Permit reminder, summary and submission'
acceptance_criteria.then: the reminder to bring their permit on the first working day is shown to every non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland (including C-permit holders) and to every employee living abroad, whatever their nationality, because nationality is not asked of them; Swiss citizens living in Switzerland do not see it. The reminder collects no answer.

examples.name: Maria, Portuguese with a C permit (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-845204)
Tomás, Brazilian with a B permit (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-b90bd9)
Swiss citizen living abroad like Stefan (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a); country of residence assumed to be Germany

acceptance_criteria.title: HR provides the reminder wording
acceptance_criteria.given: the permit reminder is to be shown
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire goes live
acceptance_criteria.then: the reminder uses wording provided by HR before go-live, phrased so that a Swiss citizen living abroad can see it does not apply to them; the spec fixes only its purpose. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: HR delivers the wording before go-live.

stories.title: Discard answers that no longer apply on submission
stories.i_want: answers I gave to questions that no longer apply after I change an earlier answer to be kept while I move back and forth, but discarded when I submit
stories.so_that: I lose no input while correcting myself, and no personal data that no party needs is kept about me
stories.priority_reason: Required by data minimisation (G-01); the keep-while-editing part is a convenience.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are kept while going back and forth
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered questions that depend on an earlier answer (for example the spouse's date of birth after answering Married)
acceptance_criteria.when: before submitting they change the earlier answer so that those questions no longer apply, and later change it back
acceptance_criteria.then: the earlier answers to those questions reappear unchanged; this is testable before submission. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers that no longer apply are discarded on submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered questions that, after a later change of an earlier answer, no longer apply to them
acceptance_criteria.when: they submit the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: those answers are discarded and are not recorded for any receiving party; only answers to questions that apply are kept.

examples.name: Employee first answered Married, then changed to Single
Employee first entered Germany, then changed the home address to Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: The same applies after an HR change
acceptance_criteria.given: a submitted questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: HR changes an answer so that some recorded answers no longer apply
acceptance_criteria.then: those answers are discarded, as on the employee's submission. How HR makes the change belongs to the later HR-side spec. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert.

stories.title: Make the questionnaire read-only after submission and derive results from the latest answers
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to be read-only for the employee once submitted, with every later change made by HR and every derived result always derived again from the latest answers
stories.so_that: a moved first working day or other change never leaves a stale result such as a wrong insurance start date at the pension fund
stories.priority_reason: A missed update of a changed first working day (Julia) caused a wrong date at the fund, an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing.

acceptance_criteria.title: Read-only for the employee after submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they open it again
acceptance_criteria.then: they can see their answers but cannot change them, and the questionnaire is never reopened for them; later changes (a move, a marriage, a new child, a certificate of residence handed in later, a corrected nationality, a new first working day) are made by HR, as specified in the later HR-side spec. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.title: Derived results always follow the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: HR has changed a recorded answer after submission, for example the first working day as in Julia's case (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-e18e66)
acceptance_criteria.when: the derived results are looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date, the civil status for the fund and for source tax, whether the employee is subject to source tax and the tariff code are derived again from the latest answers; for the first working day the latest date counts and no history of earlier dates is kept.

acceptance_criteria.title: Results needing answers never asked show 'incomplete - HR must complete'
acceptance_criteria.given: HR has changed an answer after submission so that questions now apply that the employee was never asked (for example a move from Switzerland to Germany makes the cross-border and source tax questions apply)
acceptance_criteria.when: the derived results that depend on those questions are looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: they show 'incomplete - HR must complete' instead of a value until HR enters the missing answers itself; the employee is not asked again. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert.

stories.title: Save answers as I go and resume until I submit
stories.i_want: my answers to be saved as I go so that I can stop and resume the questionnaire until I submit it
stories.so_that: I can look up details (for example my spouse's date of birth or my start date) without losing what I already entered
stories.priority_reason: Convenience for the employee; it does not block any registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are saved and the employee can resume
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered part of the questionnaire and not yet submitted it
acceptance_criteria.when: they leave and come back later
acceptance_criteria.then: their answers so far are still there and they can continue and change any answer until they submit. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.title: Nothing is recorded for the receiving parties before submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has saved but not submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they have not yet confirmed the submission
acceptance_criteria.then: the answers are not yet recorded for HR or any receiving party as submitted. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert.

stories.title: Review a summary and submit with one confirmation
stories.i_want: to see a summary of all my answers at the end and submit them with a single confirmation
stories.so_that: I can check that my information, especially my first working day, is right before it is recorded for HR
stories.priority_reason: HR wants the employee to confirm the first working day because it changes often; the summary supports this but blocks nothing on its own.

acceptance_criteria.title: Summary of the answers that apply
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered all required questions that apply to them
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach step 8 'Permit reminder, summary and submission'
acceptance_criteria.then: they see a summary of their answers to the questions that apply to them, including the first working day they confirm, and can go back to change any answer. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.title: One confirmation submits the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is on the summary in step 8 and every required question that applies is answered
acceptance_criteria.when: they confirm once
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire is submitted, the answers are recorded for HR, answers that no longer apply are discarded and the questionnaire becomes read-only for the employee. Submission is not possible while a required question that applies is unanswered. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert.
